name: US inflation
summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September, inside the Watch band; October data not yet published as of 8 Nov
state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7% in August, inside the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). It has not risen for three straight months on the latest data, and October figures had not been published as of 8 Nov. Brent was about $98 on 6 Nov, 6% lower than a month earlier (Yahoo Finance).
for_you: Higher prices weigh most on households with little spare income, and on borrowers if interest rates stay higher for longer as a result.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.0% y/y inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band; below the 4.5% Alert line
why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
